dno_dashboard.subtitle: Fragmented DSO market — ~25 operators · Codensa (Enel) + EPM + EPSA/Celsia + Air-e/Afinia + others · 32 departamentos + Bogotá D.C.
dno_dashboard.intro: Colombia's distribution sector is regionally fragmented with ~25+ distribution operators (Operadores de Red, OR) following Law 142+143/1994 sector unbundling. Codensa S.A. E.S.P. (Enel Colombia, ~30% of national DSO MWh, Bogotá D.C. + Cundinamarca) is the dominant operator. EPM (Empresa Pública de Medellín, ~municipally-owned, Antioquia) is the largest municipally-owned utility. The Caribbean coast operator Electricaribe entered intervention 2016; the territory was split in 2020 into Air-e + Afinia (under EPM management). EPSA/Celsia operates Valle del Cauca. Smaller regional operators (CHEC Caldas + EBSA Boyacá + ESSA Santander + CENS Norte de Santander + EDEQ Quindío + CEDENAR Nariño + DISPAC Chocó + ELECTROHUILA Huila + EMCALI Cali + ~10 more) cover the rest. This is the most fragmented OECD electricity distribution sector after the United States, with a mix of state-owned + municipally-owned + private-Enel + cooperative ownership models.
